naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under. A blank value counts as none.
Optional text describing the retrieval.

The document kind: `retrieval`, the reverse direction, which lands OSDU's search index as JSON Lines files on the lake. The loader chooses the reader by it and refuses a document that declares no `flowType` or `documentType`.
The retrieval flow's name: its pipeline identity. The flow id is derived from it the same way a delivery flow's is.

Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in `source.query` and `target.location`; a `target.location` token that is neither `{run}`, `{date}` nor a declared parameter is refused. Values come from `--set name=value`, the run's values, or the schedule's `values`.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.
The value used when a run supplies none.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.

The HTTP settings, as on a delivery flow (timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size), and `concurrency`: the kinds retrieved at once. `reliability.parallelInterfaces` is refused.
A delivery flow's setting: rendered documents per work batch file. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: records claimed per ledger round trip when retrying records. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
The kinds retrieved at once, each on its own search cursor. At least 1; at most 64 run at once.
A delivery flow's setting: the member runs a large submission spreads over. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: below this many records a submission never fans out. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.
A delivery source's setting: how many of its interfaces run at once. A retrieval flow runs no interfaces, so the loader refuses it here.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.

A delivery flow's setting: renderers in the intake pipeline on one node, 0 to 256 (0 takes half the machine's processors, at least one). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; a retrieval flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.
The OSDU side: the platform, the kinds and query, how the index is paged, the optional watermark, and whether full records are read back from storage.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Optional; written as `target.auth` on a delivery flow.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).

The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one).
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.

Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here.
One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent.
An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
The base URL of the OSDU platform, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`.
Storage read-backs in flight per page, each for a hundred ids. Between 1 and 64.
The index holds a projection; set this to read every hit's full record back from storage and land it as storage holds it. Ids storage cannot return are counted and listed in the manifest.
Headers sent with every request, as on a delivery flow's target. `data-partition-id` is required: every OSDU service rejects a request without it.
One header; `<name>` is the header name (`data-partition-id: dev`). A value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}).

The watermark: a run covers `[last completed run's upper bound, now minus lagMinutes)` on `field`, appended to the query. Only a completed run advances it, and `--force` restarts at `since`. Without this block every run takes everything the query matches.
The record field the window is taken on: a field path without whitespace.
How far behind now the window ends, in minutes, so records the indexer has not caught up with are left for the next run. Must not be negative.
Where the first run, and a forced run, starts: an RFC 3339 date and time such as `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Left out, the first run starts from the beginning.
One kind to retrieve, `authority:source:entityType:version` with wildcards per segment. Each kind is one search cursor.
keys.appliesWhen: Give `source.kind` (one kind) or `source.kinds` (a list); at least one kind is required, and none may repeat.

keys.description: The kinds to retrieve. Each is one search cursor, and they run concurrently up to `reliability.concurrency`. The same kind listed twice is refused.
keys.appliesWhen: Give `source.kind` (one kind) or `source.kinds` (a list); at least one kind is required.

keys.description: A kind, `authority:source:entityType:version` with wildcards per segment (`osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:1.*.*`).
Records per search page, between 1 and 1000 (the search service's cap).
The search service's info path under the endpoint. It must start with `/`.

A Lucene query narrowing the kinds, with `{parameter}` tokens substituted from the flow's parameters. An incremental flow's window is appended as `AND field:[from TO to}`. Left out, every record of the kinds is taken.
The search path the `plan` operation counts with. It must start with `/`.
The storage path that reads records back by id. It must start with `/`.
The fields to project the hits on. Empty returns whole hits.
One field of a hit to return.
The cursor search path the retrieve operation pages through. It must start with `/`.
The lake side: where a run's files and manifest go and how the files are cut. A run's directory holds a directory per kind and the manifest.
How the files are compressed: `none` writes `part-00001.jsonl`, `gzip` writes `part-00001.jsonl.gz`.
The file format. A retrieval writes JSON Lines; any other value is refused.

The run's directory root: a local path or a storage URI, with `{parameter}`, `{run}` and `{date}` tokens; any other token is refused. Without a `{run}` token every run gets a timestamped directory beneath it, so runs never overwrite each other. A relative local path is resolved against the working directory of the process running the flow, so the repository sync warns about one: use an absolute path or a storage URI.

The manifest's file name inside the run's directory, not a path (`/` and `\` are refused). The manifest names the flow, the run, the window, every file with its record count and uncompressed bytes, and per kind the records storage could not read back.
A new file every this many records (`part-00001`, `part-00002`, ...) under a directory named after the kind. At least 1.
